passage.label: Al-Ma'idah — Allah asks Isa did you tell people take me mother deities besides Allah; Isa says exalted You not for me say without right; if said You would know; You know what in myself I not know what in Yourself You Knower unseen; said only what commanded worship Allah my Lord your Lord; was witness over them while among them; when took me You were Watcher over them You Witness all things; if punish they Your servants; if forgive You Exalted Wise; Allah says this Day truthfulness benefits truthful; gardens rivers flowing abiding forever; Allah pleased with them they pleased with Him great attainment; to Allah dominion heavens earth whatever in them He over all things Capable

arabicExcerpts.text: وَإِذۡ قَالَ ٱللَّهُ يَٰعِيسَى ٱبۡنَ مَرۡيَمَ ءَأَنتَ قُلۡتَ لِلنَّاسِ ٱتَّخِذُونِي وَأُمِّيَ إِلَٰهَيۡنِ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِۖ قَالَ سُبۡحَٰنَكَ مَا يَكُونُ لِيٓ أَنۡ أَقُولَ مَا لَيۡسَ لِي بِحَقٍّۚ إِن كُنتُ قُلۡتُهُۥ فَقَدۡ عَلِمۡتَهُۥۚ تَعۡلَمُ مَا فِي نَفۡسِي وَلَآ أَعۡلَمُ مَا فِي نَفۡسِكَۚ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ عَلَّـٰمُ ٱلۡغُيُوبِ

مَا قُلۡتُ لَهُمۡ إِلَّا مَآ أَمَرۡتَنِي بِهِۦٓ أَنِ ٱعۡبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ رَبِّي وَرَبَّكُمۡۚ وَكُنتُ عَلَيۡهِمۡ شَهِيدٗا مَّا دُمۡتُ فِيهِمۡۖ فَلَمَّا تَوَفَّيۡتَنِي كُنتَ أَنتَ ٱلرَّقِيبَ عَلَيۡهِمۡۚ وَأَنتَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءٖ شَهِيدٌ
إِن تُعَذِّبۡهُمۡ فَإِنَّهُمۡ عِبَادُكَۖ وَإِن تَغۡفِرۡ لَهُمۡ فَإِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ

قَالَ ٱللَّهُ هَٰذَا يَوۡمُ يَنفَعُ ٱلصَّـٰدِقِينَ صِدۡقُهُمۡۚ لَهُمۡ جَنَّـٰتٞ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَآ أَبَدٗاۖ رَّضِيَ ٱللَّهُ عَنۡهُمۡ وَرَضُواْ عَنۡهُۚ ذَٰلِكَ ٱلۡفَوۡزُ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ
لِلَّهِ مُلۡكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا فِيهِنَّۚ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءٖ قَدِيرُۢ

mainSubject.label: Isa's eschatological denial of commanding worship of himself and mother; affirmation of exclusive tawheed message (worship Allah my Lord and your Lord); Isa as temporary witness replaced by divine Watcher after his departure; divine prerogative of punishment-forgiveness balanced with servant-status acknowledgment; truthfulness rewarded with eternal gardens and mutual divine-human pleasure; closing declaration of absolute divine dominion and capability

subordinateSubjects.label: Divine interrogation of Isa regarding alleged divinity claim
Isa's exaltation-response: subhanaka denying unauthorized speech
Asymmetric knowledge: You know my self I do not know Yours
Isa's message limited to commanded tawheed: worship Allah my Lord your Lord
Isa as witness during earthly presence; Allah as Raqeeb after departure
Divine prerogative: punishment or forgiveness both justified
Servant-status acknowledgment: they are Your servants
Eternal gardens with rivers as reward for truthful
Mutual pleasure: Allah pleased with them they pleased with Him
Great attainment (fawz azim) as ultimate success designation
Absolute divine dominion over heavens earth and all within
Divine capability over all things as closing declaration

divineNamesAndAttributes.gloss: the Exalted Mighty the Wise (editorial gloss)

propheticNarratives.label: Isa's eschatological testimony denying divinity claims and affirming tawheed-only message

humanConditionsAndSpiritualStates.label: Truthfulness (sidq) as salvific quality benefiting its possessor on Judgment Day
Mutual divine-human pleasure as highest relational state in Paradise

relationships.label: Creator-servant relationship affirmed even in intercessory context: they are Your servants

notes: Pass A Maidah passage 14/14. Final Christological correction and surah closure. Isa's three-part denial (subhanaka + ma yakoonu lee + in kuntu qultuhu) provides comprehensive refutation template. Asymmetric-knowledge argument (taAAlamu ma fee nafsee wala aAAlamu ma fee nafsika) establishes ontological gap proving creaturely status. Raqeeb-Witness transition (5:117) clarifies prophetic temporality versus divine permanence. Servant-status framing (5:118) prevents intercession from implying independent authority. Mutual-pleasure formula (radiya Allahu AAanhum waradoo AAanhu) represents peak Quranic salvation language. Dominion-capability closure (5:120) echoes surah opening themes completing literary ring structure.
